Research dossier: FN — Fabrinet

Researched: 2026-07-04 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.65 · Opportunity score: 68

Next earnings: 2026-08-24

Business

Thailand-based precision contract manufacturer of optical and electro-mechanical packages —

the company that physically assembles and tests high-speed optical transceivers (800G now,

1.6T ramping) and related photonics for other people's brands. Customers are the optical/

networking primes and, increasingly, the chip vendor itself: NVIDIA (~30% of revenue, sell-side

sees up to ~50% annualized), plus Cisco, Coherent, Lumentum, Ciena, and a named direct

hyperscaler relationship (AWS, plus two newer direct datacom programs ramping through FY27).

FN reportedly holds ~100% market share on the 1.6T transceivers feeding NVIDIA's Blackwell

platform. Revenue durably continues because FN owns scarce precision-manufacturing capacity

and yield/quality entrenchment that primes don't want to rebuild — they design the optics, FN

builds them. It is a substrate / picks-and-shovels play in the

orchestration-vs-substrate frame: real earnings, but thin (~10% net) contract-manufacturing

margins and limited IP/pricing power. Unchanged since the last dive.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

Nothing about the business changed in the last week; the price did — a lot. Since the 6/27

dossier (BUY at $524.79, small starter), the cohort de-rate that dossier called **deepened

further: FN closed $499.61 on 7/2** (screen shows $500.29), down another ~5% from 6/27 and

now 33.0% off its 52-week high, ret_20d -31.0%, ret_60d flipped to -10.3% (was +0.7%

three weeks ago), and — the one genuinely new technical fact — -3.7% vs. the 200DMA, meaning

price has now broken through the 200-day uptrend line it was sitting on top of at the last

dive. The driver is the same cohort story, just a second leg: AAOI -17%, COHR -10%, LITE -10%

around 7/1-7/2 on no name-specific news, tied to the broader AI-infra/semis "valuation

reckoning" the macro read has been tracking since 6/23, sharpened by the Meta Compute report

(hyperscaler capex-competition fear, not a demand cut — capex guides are still +77% YoY per

ai-infra-thesis-kill-switches). No FN-specific bad news surfaced in this run: no new

downgrade, no guidance change, no CPO-bypass signal. The Raytek/CPO integration and the two

direct-hyperscaler datacom programs from the last dive stand unchanged and un-contradicted.

Per macro-cohort-confirmation, a second cohort-wide leg down with no idiosyncratic news is

still liquidity, not information — the thesis is not weaker, the price is just cheaper. The

prior dossier explicitly pre-committed: *"a further cohort-wide leg to ~$500 ... → add (better

entry, same thesis)."* That is exactly what has happened. **BUY, add toward the lower end of the

range — this is the add, not a fresh idea.**

Valuation + position vs. range

  • Price ~$500 ($499.61 close 7/2, screen $500.29); market cap $17.90B; 52-wk range

$272.49–$748.89 (off-high 33.0%, +82.8% above the low). ret_20d -31.0%, ret_60d

-10.3%, -22.1% vs 50DMA, -3.7% vs 200DMA — the pullback has now cut through the

200-day trend line, not just approached it.

  • Trailing P/E 42.9-45.1 (sources vary slightly on TTM window), forward P/E 30.49

(compressed from 32.0 three weeks ago, and now essentially at the floor of my fair band).

Revenue TTM $4.24B (+29.8%); net income TTM $420.97M (+29.0%); EPS TTM $11.64;

~35.83M shares (low float — amplifies moves both ways). Implied forward EPS ~$16.4

NTM, unchanged.

  • My fair-value read, unchanged from last dive: 30–35× forward on a ~30%-grower with

single-customer concentration and a CPO hedge (Raytek) → $492–$574. At ~$500 the market

pays ~30.5× NTM — the bottom of the band, not the midpoint anymore. Sell-side is far more

bullish: average 12-month PT $763.67 (5 Buy / 2 Hold, high $850 / low $680, per Benzinga),

which itself signals the Street still treats this as a growth name at a discount, not a

broken one. PEG still ~1.0 on ~30% growth, and FN remains the **cheapest real-earnings name in

its cohort** (COHR, LITE both trade at multiples several times FN's).

Post-deal / repriced check

Not a Wait-for-deal thesis name, but the repriced discipline still applies and has moved

further in the buyer's favor since 6/27: the de-rate that had "fully opened" at $525 has now

overshot toward the bottom of my fair band, still with no fundamentally new negative

information. This is the second, deeper wave of the same de-rate, not a new distinct event —

worth flagging because two consecutive cohort legs down raises the question of whether this is

becoming a structural repricing rather than a one-off dip. Kill-switches (capex, GPU pricing,

credit spreads) are all still clear per state/research/macro.md, and credit spreads showed

zero reaction to either leg — the strongest evidence this remains a narrow equity-multiple

repricing, not new information about the business. The edge is un-consumed, arguably more open

than three weeks ago.

Council (one line each, no hedging)

  • Bull: Sole-scale assembler of the exact 1.6T optics the AI buildout needs at ~100%

Blackwell share, +39% and accelerating, now winning direct hyperscaler programs AND holding a

CPO foothold via Raytek — priced at 30.5× forward, the bottom of a reasonable band, after two

consecutive cohort-wide de-rate legs with zero FN-specific bad news and Street targets still

~50% above spot.

  • Bear: A ~10%-margin contract manufacturer with 30-50% of revenue on one customer, in a

cohort now on its second leg of a "valuation reckoning" — two legs down instead of one is

exactly the pattern that precedes a name breaking its 200DMA for real and staying broken; CPO

still structurally threatens pluggables and Raytek is a hedge, not a guaranteed mandate.

  • First-principles: A capacity-and-yield business with no IP moat and one dominant customer

is worth ~30-35× only while the pluggable cycle and that customer's volume hold — at 30.5×

fwd with +39% growth, two cohort-confirmed dip legs, and no fundamental deterioration, the

price is now paying you more than fair for the concentration risk, not merely fair.

  • Fair: ~$540 (≈33× forward, re-derived slightly below the last dive's $550 given the

further multiple compression across the cohort).

  • Stretch: ~$580 (≈35.5× forward; above here you're re-paying for froth with no new

catalyst).

  • Add-lower: ~$470 (≈29× forward, below the low end of the fair band) — scale further if a

third cohort leg materializes; below this the "structural repricing, not a dip" bear case

needs to be taken seriously and the position re-underwritten, not just averaged down.

  • Current ~$500 sits inside the buy-below zone, at the level the prior dossier flagged as

the trigger for adding. Base rates (patterns.py, unchanged): dip_buyer preset ACTIVE — +63d

win 71.7%, avg +17.0%, worst -23.9%, avg drawdown -10.2% (56 instances);

extended_run weaker (+63d avg +13.1%, worst -30.2%). The dip shape still has the edge; the

Macro fit

Kill-switches all clear (capex +77% YoY confirmed unchanged per 7/4 macro read; GPU

pricing/lead-times firm at the frontier tier; HY OAS ~276-278bp, flat and near 25-year tights —

zero credit reaction to either optics-cohort leg down). FN remains less rate-sensitive than the

extreme-P/S cohort because it has real earnings (~4× P/S, 30.5× fwd P/E) — the Warsh

hawkish-hold dot plot is a moderate multiple headwind here, not the acute one facing no-earnings

names. Macro stance is "hold cash; buy only real dips or fresh catalysts, small size, prefer

names below/at fair value, cohort-confirm before adding to single names." FN satisfies all of

that more cleanly than three weeks ago: the dip is now deeper and still cohort-confirmed

(AAOI/COHR/LITE all down again the same days, no FN-specific news), and price has moved from

mid-band to the bottom of my fair-value band. On the Opportunity-cost lens this is one of

the few names in the field getting objectively cheaper on a real growth story with clear

macro-level (not name-level) cause. Score raised to 68 (from 65): deeper cohort-confirmed

dip into the bottom of the fair band (+), zero new FN-specific negative information across two

legs (+), Street targets unchanged and well above spot (+) — capped below 75+ because the

200DMA break and the second consecutive cohort leg are genuinely new risk (a third leg would

force re-underwriting the "de-rate vs. structural reset" question), and the single-customer/CPO

overhang remains live. Sizing: add at ≤$510, toward ~$470 if the cohort extends further; per

catalyst-payoff-shape-sizing the left tail still caps clip size even as the entry improves.

Falsification

  • 30-day: A third cohort-wide leg to ~$470 with the group still moving together (per

macro-cohort-confirmation) → add again, same thesis, better price. A bounce back above

~$580 with no new catalyst → stop adding, edge re-consumed. Any FN-specific bad news (a real

NVIDIA-share loss, a margin warning, a CPO-bypass confirmation) at any price → reassess to

HOLD/AVOID immediately, not add.

  • 60-day (Aug 24 print): Q4 FY26 must confirm the 1.6T ramp, the two direct-hyperscaler

programs actually shipping revenue, and hold/expand the ~10% margin. A guide-down, margin

compression, or softening NVIDIA-share commentary → AVOID regardless of price.

  • 90-day: A concrete CPO adoption signal that bypasses FN (a hyperscaler/NVIDIA CPO switch

deployment whose optical engines FN — including via Raytek — does not build) remains the

single most important structural watch item, unchanged from the last dive. Conversely, FN

landing the CPO optical-engine assembly mandate or a third named direct-hyperscaler program

would re-rate the durability case and lift fair value materially above the current band.

Research dossier: MOD — Modine Manufacturing Company

Researched: 2026-07-04 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.6 · Opportunity score: 66

Next earnings: 2026-08-05 (one estimate puts it 2026-07-29; treat as unconfirmed until IR

posts the date — Q1 FY27, first print with the new "Data Centers" reporting segment)

Business

Modine makes thermal-management hardware — heat exchangers, coils, chillers, and

coolant-distribution units (CDUs). Two legacy legs: Climate Solutions (HVAC&R, heating, and

the fast-growing data-center cooling line) and Performance Technologies (cyclical

auto/commercial-vehicle thermal), which is being spun off. Data-center customers (hyperscalers +

colo) pay Modine because liquid cooling is on the critical path to energizing dense GPU racks —

a direct, picks-and-shovels lever on the same hyperscaler capex the macro kill-switches track

(~$700–725B 2026, +77% YoY, still supply-constrained).

Structural change in flight, timeline update: the Gentherm (THRM) Reverse Morris Trust —

Modine keeps ~$210M cash, holders get ~21M THRM shares (~40% of combined co) — is confirmed but

this run's sources put closing "targeted for Q4 2026", later and vaguer than the prior

dossier's "effective 2026-09-01." Regulatory clearance, Gentherm shareholder vote, and IRS tax

opinion are all still open contingencies per the 425 filing. Treat the Sept-1 date as stale;

timeline risk is now a live, not resolved, watch item.

Fresh thesis — what changed since the 2026-06-27 dossier

The prior dive called a trigger-gated BUY at ~$255 with buy-below $238. Price has since fallen

further to $231.06 (2026-07-04 close context; -5.5% on 7/2 alone) with **no new negative

fact about Modine specifically** — this is the same continuation of the post-print

profit-taking/de-rating, not a fresh bear catalyst. Two confirms on that read:

1. Cohort confirmation (macro-cohort-confirmation): Vertiv (the closest DC-cooling

comp) fell ~11% in a single July session and ~25-26% through June on the same

"profit-taking in expensive AI-infra winners" dynamic — sector-wide multiple compression,

not a Modine-specific break. This is exactly the check the framework asks for before

buying a dip.

2. Analyst targets moved UP, not down, into the weakness: KeyBanc raised PT to $370 (from

$250), UBS to $355 (from $310), consensus avg now ~$341 (8 analysts, "Strong Buy",

~48% implied upside from spot). Sell-side conviction on the fundamentals did not follow

the stock down — a genuine divergence, not just stale coverage (these are dated after the

Q4 print and reflect the guide).

One new fact that is a real, if contained, negative: Modine disclosed component shortages

(key inputs for DC cooling products, first appearing in Q4 FY26) that are **temporarily

capping the DC capacity ramp** while the company qualifies new vendors. Management says it does

not expect this to hit full-year production, and the FY27 guide (sales +20-35%, DC +60-80%,

EBITDA $650-680M) is unchanged as of the last confirmed statement — this is a demand-outpacing-

supply problem (bullish signal on demand, bearish on near-term execution), not a demand

problem. Worth tracking into Aug print, not yet thesis-breaking.

Insider selling continues (VP/CHRO, a director, and the Data Centers president sold in

June, mostly under pre-set Rule 10b5-1 plans) — normal at this share-price level for a stock

up multiples off its 52-week low, and it's the same signal the prior dossier already noted;

not incrementally worse. Partial offset: CEO Brinker and CFO Lucareli bought shares May 20,

six days ahead of the Q4 print.

Valuation + position vs. range

  • Price ~$230-231; market cap ~$12.2B (down from ~$13.5B on 6/27).
  • TTM revenue $3.18B (+23.1%); EPS $2.26. Trailing P/E ~102 (from ~113), **forward P/E

~29.6x** (from ~32.8x) — the multiple has compressed further even as guidance held, which is

the setup this framework wants: price falling, thesis unchanged.

  • 52-week range $86.49–$323.25. Screen: off_52w_high 28.3%, above_52w_low 166.8%, ret_20d

-23.5%, ret_60d +7.9%, vs_50dma -14.4%, vs_200dma +17.1% — a materially deeper pullback than

the 6/27 read (off-high was 20.7% then), still well above the 200dma (structurally intact

uptrend, tactically oversold on the 50dma).

  • GuruFocus's GF Value model flags MOD as ~90%+ "overvalued" (GF Value ~$137 vs. price

~$230-267 across late June prints) — a mechanical mean-reversion/DCF model that doesn't

price in the DC pivot or the $4B contracted floor; I weight this near zero against a

forward-earnings-anchored read, but note it as the bear's best off-the-shelf number.

  • My fair-value read: ~$255-275 on FY27 numbers, unchanged from the prior dive (the guide

hasn't moved) — meaning today's $231 sits ~10-15% below my own fair value, a real

discount that didn't exist on 6/27 (then it was "about fairly valued").

Post-deal / repriced check

Per Wait-for-deal thesis: the $4B chiller deal already landed (5/26) and the entry edge

from that specific catalyst is consumed — but per extended-with-vs-without-catalyst, the

question for the pullback is different: has anything happened in the last 7 days that breaks

the post-deal thesis? No. The component-shortage disclosure is a near-term execution wrinkle

already flagged by management as temporary; the RMT timeline slipping from "Sept 1" to "Q4

Opportunity-cost lens rotation out of AI-infra winners, confirmed by VRT falling in

parallel — this is the "real dip, no negative fact" case the macro read explicitly says to

re-engage on.

Council (one line each, no hedging)

  • Bull: Thesis, guide, and analyst targets are all unchanged-to-better while the stock is

down another ~9% on cohort rotation — a wider discount to fair value than three weeks ago

with no new reason for it.

Macro fit

Kill-switches all clear (capex accelerating $700-725B/+77%, GPU pricing firm at the frontier

tier, HY OAS ~276-278bp, all unchanged per today's macro re-read). MOD remains the right shape

for a hawkish-Fed regime: earnings-anchored (~29.6x forward, not a terminal-multiple bet), so it

sidesteps the discount-rate sizing penalty pinning NBIS/IREN/extreme-P/S names. On the

Opportunity-cost lens it now ranks higher than three weeks ago — same thesis, cheaper

Research dossier: APLD — Applied Digital Corporation

Researched: 2026-07-03 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.55 · Opportunity score: 62

Business

Applied Digital builds and leases hyperscale AI/HPC data center campuses — a compute-infrastructure

landlord, not a cloud/GPU-rental operator (that business, Applied Digital's old bitcoin-hosting +

cloud-services lines, is now a rounding error next to the AI Factory leasing segment). The model:

acquire land + power interconnect in North Dakota/Texas-belt sites, build shell-and-core + power/

cooling infrastructure, sign long-term (15-year) triple-net-style take-or-pay leases with

investment-grade hyperscaler tenants for the critical IT load, and collect rent once each building

reaches Ready-for-Service (RFS). Revenue is contracted years before it's recognized — the backlog

is the business. As of early July 2026: 5 campuses (Polaris Forge 1 & 3, Delta Forge 1 & 2,

plus the original Ellendale/Harwood ND footprint), **1.4GW of contracted critical IT load / 2.15GW

of grid power, ~$36B base-term contracted revenue / ~$86B if all renewal options exercise**,

~70% of contracted revenue backed by US investment-grade hyperscalers. TTM revenue is only

$319M (+66% YoY) — the gap between $319M booked and $36B backed is the entire investment case: this

is early-innings monetization of an already-signed, already-investment-grade backlog, not a

speculative pipeline.

Who pays: undisclosed-by-name but described as "US-based, high investment-grade hyperscaler(s)" for

Delta Forge 2 ($5.2B/15-yr, 210MW, RFS ~1Q28) and Polaris Forge 3 ($7.5B base/$18.2B full, 300MW,

RFS ~Aug 2027) — plus CoreWeave at Polaris Forge 1 (150MW lease, now being restructured through a

CoreWeave special-purpose-vehicle subsidiary carrying an A3/Moody's-rated project facility, backed

by a springing parent guarantee and a $50M letter of credit — converting CoreWeave's non-investment-

grade (BB) parent credit into IG-rated project financing for APLD's own construction debt). Why the

revenue durably continues: 15-year take-or-pay leases with early-termination economics that make

walking away far more expensive than paying rent, IG counterparties, and — per

permitting-as-binding-constraint — APLD sits on the already-permitted side of the ledger

(Delta Forge 1 named explicitly in that framework), which is a scarcity premium every new local

moratorium elsewhere makes more valuable, not less.

high) while the fundamental tape over the same six weeks has been the best stretch in the

company's history: two new hyperscaler leases signed (Delta Forge 2 6/8, Polaris Forge 3 6/8-9,

lifting base backlog from ~$23.5B/3 campuses in May to ~$36B/5 campuses now), the CoreWeave lease

restructured onto an IG-rated SPV (lowers APLD's own project-debt cost), and Polaris Forge 1

Building 2 Phase-1 delivered RFS on schedule on 7/1 (75MW, 175MW now live at that campus alone).

No analyst has downgraded the name or cut a target through this drawdown — Northland ($82),

NVIDIA sells the accelerated-compute substrate for AI: data-center GPUs (Blackwell B200/B300,

question that matters for the valuation, and it rests on two legs: (a) hyperscaler capex

continuing to ramp, and (b) GPU economics — rental price and useful life — staying firm. Both

are still standing, but both took a knock this month (see below).

valuation is the most attractive it's been: Q1 FY27 (2026-05-20) was a real acceleration —

revenue $81.6B (+85% YoY), Data Center a record $75.2B (+92%), and Q2 guided to $91B

zeroed from the run-rate (pure upside optionality). None of that has broken.

What changed since the 2026-06-13 dossier, and why I'm marking down:

  • The catalyst went stale. The May-20 print is now 5+ weeks old. The macro discipline

the AI dollar downward, which is a signal, not just noise.

Nvidia - AI Cycle Durability essay's counter still holds — GPUs win on useful-life/financing

durability question now has a real, market-visible data point against it, which the prior

dossier underweighted.

  • GPU cloud-rental is softening (kill-switch #2 yellow flag, NOT tripped — see Macro fit).

Research dossier: FSLR — First Solar

Researched: 2026-07-03 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.55 · Opportunity score: 58

Next earnings: 2026-07-23

Business

First Solar is the largest US-domiciled solar module maker, building thin-film cadmium-telluride (CdTe) panels rather than the polysilicon modules that dominate globally — a technology that structurally sidesteps the silicon trade war and the pending Section 232 polysilicon case. Revenue is ~96% US, from domestic fabs in Ohio, Alabama, and Louisiana plus older Malaysia/Vietnam capacity now running at deliberately low utilization (~20%) to avoid reciprocal tariffs. Customers are utility-scale developers and corporate clean-energy buyers on multi-year, fixed-price, take-or-pay contracts. The P&L rides two US policy levers: (1) Section 45X manufacturing credits (~$0.17/W thin-film; FY26 EBITDA guide $2.6–2.8B is still credit-heavy), sold for cash (>$2.0B transferred to date); (2) tariffs (Section 201 expired Feb 2026; 301/AD-CVD plus a pending Section 232 polysilicon case) that wall off Chinese/SE-Asian supply. Demand durability is real (contracted backlog + AI-driven electricity growth); the risk is concentrated in policy and litigation overhang, not end-demand.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

The 2026-06-25 dossier held HOLD with a derived buy-below of $236 and said the gate ("real dip OR fresh catalyst") was "almost met, not met." Nine trading days later, the price has done what that dossier said would flip it: **FSLR closed 7/2 at $224.57, now −29.9% off its 52-week high and, for the first time in this dossier's history, trading below both its 50dma (~$245) and 200dma (~$235) — a materially deeper dip than the "into the DMA cluster" read three weeks ago. On the framework's own terms this is a real dip**, not a stale anchor to re-litigate.

What's new since 6/25, and it's a mixed bag:

1. A securities class action was filed (Pomerantz, ~6/29; Robbins Geller, Faruqi & Faruqi, Rosen, Kaplan Fox, Levi & Korsinsky all piling on with lead-plaintiff-deadline alerts, deadline 8/24/26). Docket 26-cv-03787 (EDNY). Alleges FSLR overstated its ability to manage 2025 tariff policy and understated how badly the intentional ~20%-utilization idling of the Malaysia/Vietnam lines would hit FY26 results, class period 2/26/25–2/24/26. This is backward-looking — it re-litigates the already-known Feb 2026 guidance disappointment (guide cut ~14% on the print) rather than surfacing new fundamental deterioration, but it adds a real (if likely bounded, given FSLR's balance sheet) legal-cost/reputational overhang that will run for months.

2. Heavy, one-directional insider selling — 135 insider transactions in 6 months, 0 buys, 135 sells, including CEO Widmar (39,951 shares). This predates the lawsuit and doesn't by itself prove new bad news, but it's a bearish tell that management isn't using the drawdown to signal confidence — worth naming, not dismissing.

3. Section 232 polysilicon ruling is now genuinely imminent, not just "pending." Industry trade sources (pv-tech, pv-magazine) now peg July 4, 2026 as the widely-expected announcement date — i.e., the binary the 6/25 dossier flagged as the "fresh catalyst that would flip this to BUY" could resolve within days of this research date. CdTe (FSLR's tech) is insulated from a polysilicon tariff/quota; a favorable ruling raises the cost of Chinese-linked crystalline-silicon competition.

4. TOPCon patent fight is offensive, not defensive, for FSLR — the ITC Section 337 case (337-TA-1494) is First Solar suing ~47 entities (Trina, JinkoSolar-linked importers, etc.) over TOPCon patents; Tesla and BYD America have intervened as downstream buyers exposed to a possible import restriction. A win narrows competitor US market access — a moat reinforcement, not a liability, contrary to how some coverage frames it as "uncertainty."

5. The OBBBA excise-tax scare resolved in solar's favor cohort-wide (per this pipeline's own 7/1 NXT resolved-thread finding): the punitive FEOC excise tax in the 6/27 Senate draft did not survive to the final bill text, and the cohort rallied on relief 6/30–7/1. FSLR's price kept falling into and past that relief rally — the drawdown here is more idiosyncratic (lawsuit + insider selling) than pure cohort/macro, which matters for macro-cohort-confirmation: this is not a clean "buy the cohort dip" case, it's "buy despite a name-specific legal overhang that the fundamentals don't support as a repricing of the business."

Net: valuation is now cheaper than the 6/25 read (P/E 14.5 / fwd P/E 11.7 vs. 16.1/12.9), the price is through my own prior buy-below and below both DMAs, the 45X credit legislative durability from the 6/25 read is unchanged, and a real unfired catalyst (Section 232) is due literally any day. The offsetting news (lawsuit, insider selling) is real but doesn't touch the core 45X/backlog thesis — it's headline and governance-signal risk, not a demand or credit break. That tips this from HOLD to a modest-conviction BUY at the prevailing price, sized small given the litigation/insider-selling overhang and the still-hawkish macro tape.

structural change is HBM as a discrete, high-ASP sub-market driven by GPU training/inference.

Micron is #3 in HBM (~21% share vs SK Hynix ~62%, Samsung ~17%) but is NVIDIA's swing supplier for

quarter just reported, and cloud memory revenue is up over 300%.

drivers/couriers are the two sides, and Uber One (~50M members, >50% of bookings) is the retention

flywheel. Durability rests on the marketplace moat: two-sided liquidity (199M MAPCs, +17% YoY)

compounds with scale and monetizes whoever supplies the ride — including third-party AV fleets.

The franchise is now structurally FCF-generative ($2.3B FCF in Q1 alone), not a cash-burner.

Research dossier: RKLB — Rocket Lab Corporation

Researched: 2026-07-07 · Verdict: BUY · Conviction: 0.50 · Opportunity score: 52

Next earnings: 2026-08-06

Business

Vertically-integrated space prime — the only credible Western reusable-launch challenger to

SpaceX. Two segments: Launch (Electron, 91+ flights all-time, 12+ in 2026; HASTE suborbital

variant; Neutron, medium-lift reusable, targeting Q4 2026 first flight, five commercial

contracts signed) and Space Systems (satellites, buses, components, solar, separation

systems, flight software — the majority of revenue). Customers pay for rides to orbit

(commercial, civil, increasingly defense — Space Force, SDA, NRO, NASA) and for the hardware

that flies on them. On 2026-06-29 the company agreed to acquire Iridium Communications for

~$8.0B EV ($27 cash + collared stock per Iridium share, collar $67.50–$112.50/RKLB share),

converting the business from a launch/components prime into a vertically-integrated space+satcom

operator with owned L-band spectrum and a 2.55M-subscriber constellation. Expected close

mid-2027.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

**Yes, tentatively — the post-deal air pocket has round-tripped price back into (and now

slightly below) the pre-Iridium entry zone, and the one number everyone was afraid of

(dilution) computes far smaller than the unconfirmed ~33% estimate that was circulating.**

Sequence since the last two dives: RKLB popped +16% to $98.01 on 6/29 (KeyBanc upgrade + the

Iridium announcement), continued to $100.46 by 7/4, then gave essentially all of that back —

$93.37 on 7/6 (-7%, "digesting the deal-driven run-up... rotating out of higher-beta space

stocks," compounded by **CEO Peter Beck filing to sell 5M shares (~$465M, ~0.9% of shares

out)** the day after the deal announcement — a real insider-selling signal, not nothing, though

sized modestly and sourced from 2021 SPAC-merger shares) — and then **$83.41 today (7/7,

-10.4%)**, dragged down with the broader chip/semi complex on the Samsung Q2 revenue-miss

selloff (per state/research/macro.md: SOX -6% to -11% intraday, Micron -4.7%, SK Hynix -9%+).

RKLB's beta (2.55) means it rides the market's AI-demand-scare tape even though satcom/launch

isn't a hyperscaler-capex name — this piece of today's move is market beta, not company news.

Net: the stock is down ~17% from Friday's $100.46 close in three sessions, on a mix of (1)

legitimate profit-taking after an unearned pop, (2) a real but modest insider-sale signal, (3) a

fair analyst debate about post-merger growth mix (blended growth reportedly drops from ~42% to

~22% once Iridium's slower-growing, but profitable, revenue base consolidates — a genuine

re-rating input, not noise), and (4) indiscriminate beta-driven selling in a broad chip scare

unrelated to RKLB's own fundamentals. None of that is a Neutron-execution or Space-Systems

problem — nothing in the underlying launch/backlog story broke this week.

The crux variable from the 7/4 user dive — dilution — I can now bound with real numbers.

Iridium has ~105.7M shares outstanding (10-Q, 2026-03-23). At today's $83.41 (inside the

Research dossier: MDB — MongoDB, Inc.

Researched: 2026-06-30 · Verdict: HOLD · Conviction: 0.57 · Opportunity score: 50

Business

MongoDB sells a document-oriented database platform. Two revenue buckets:

  • Atlas (cloud-managed, consumption-based) — the growth engine, ~75% of total revenue,

grew 29.4% YoY in Q1 FY2027 and added a record $117M of dollar net-new ARR in one quarter

(four straight quarters of >29% growth). Multi-cloud, serverless, with vector search,

text/time-series search, and stream processing folded in natively — the bet is collapsing a

separate vector store + operational DB + feature store into one managed surface, and becoming

the persistent-state layer for AI agents going to production. (orchestration-vs-substrate:

MDB is an orchestration-side data layer, not GPU substrate — its AI exposure is workload

demand, not the capex J-curve.)

  • Enterprise Advanced + Other (self-managed license + support) — mature, ~+13% YoY,

high-margin, declining share of mix.

Who pays: dev-centric enterprises building modern apps — fintech, e-commerce, gaming, real-time

personalization, AI-agent backends. The document model's schema flexibility fits when data shape

evolves fast (i.e. every AI product in production). Atlas is sticky once pipelines are built on

it. Durability: high.

Last print — Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended 2026-04-30): revenue $687.6M (+25% YoY), an

acceleration from the ~22% trough; non-GAAP op margin 18% (up from 16%); non-GAAP EPS

$1.32 (vs $1.18 est.); a small GAAP net income of +$4.4M (TTM GAAP still −$29M). TTM

revenue $2.60B (+23.6%). No new print since — the next data point is the Aug 27 Q2 report,

so fundamentals are unchanged from the May 28 print.

Elastic is an enterprise search, observability, and security platform company built on the ELK stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana). Three pillars: (1) Search — hybrid keyword + vector search, now marketed as "The Search AI Company" powering enterprise RAG applications; (2) Observability — log analytics, APM, infrastructure monitoring; (3) Security — SIEM/XDR. Revenue is >90% subscription, ~80% sales-led. Customers are deeply embedded: the ELK stack is load-bearing infrastructure for search and logging across thousands of enterprises; migration costs are high.

FY2026 full-year revenue: $1.739B (+17% YoY). $100k+ ACV customers: 1,660+. $1M+ ACV customers: >240. Net Expansion Rate: ~112%. AI use cases now penetrate >1/3 of the $100k ACV cohort; AI-using cohorts expand ~5% faster than baseline. AI backlog: >$1B as of Q4 FY26 (May 2026 report).

Why revenue continues: The installed base is structurally sticky (search indices, log pipelines, SIEM rules are not moved lightly). The enterprise-sales motion is converting larger multi-year deals — record $1M+ deal quarter in Q4 FY26, and customers with $5M+ ACV growing ~30% YoY. The platform bet (one vendor for search + observability + security) creates consolidation tailwinds vs. running three point solutions.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

As of June 8, 2026 — 12 days after Q4 FY26 earnings — the answer is: compelling valuation, awkward timing; wait for a cleaner entry.

The business case is genuine:

  • FY27 revenue guidance: $1.985–$2.0B (~15% YoY). Non-GAAP operating margin guided to ~19% (targeting 25% by FY29). FCF margin ~21.5% in FY27 → ~$430M free cash flow on a $6.35B market cap = ~6.8% FCF yield. For a 15% grower with margin expansion, this is dramatically cheap vs. software peers.
  • EV/forward sales: ~2.7x (peer group: Datadog ~10x, CrowdStrike ~18x, MongoDB ~10x). Even applying a steep discount for Elastic's competitive pressures, 3x the current multiple is defensible.
  • AI search positioning is real. Hybrid search (keyword + vector) is the dominant enterprise pattern for RAG applications — Elastic has been doing hybrid search longer than the pure vector DB startups. The $1B+ AI backlog gives near-term revenue visibility.

The timing tension: the Q4 FY26 beat (revenue $451M vs. ~$440M estimate, profitability turn, FY27 guidance) already landed on May 27 and the stock popped +24% from ~$50 to ~$62. That catalyst has been absorbed. The principles mandate: "demand a real dip OR a fresh catalyst." At $62 post-bounce, neither condition is cleanly met. A macro-induced pullback to $52-58 would restore the asymmetry needed to justify a new buy.

Conclusion: fine business, real value, not the right moment to add at $62. HOLD; watch for the re-entry.

Business

GE Vernova (spun from GE, April 2024) is the energy-technology company with three segments:

2. Electrification (~$13.9B projected 2026, +44% YoY) — grid transformers, switchgear, HVDC systems, software. Data-center-driven demand is the growth engine: $2.4B in data-center equipment orders in Q1 2026 alone, more than all of 2025 combined. Book-to-bill ~2.5x.

3. Wind (~$7B) — offshore and onshore wind; still margin-challenged but improving. Not the thesis driver; margin drag remains.

Who pays them: utilities, hyperscalers, independent power producers, grid operators globally. Power and Electrification revenue is long-cycle (backlog → execution over 3–5 years). Services contracts on installed base provide a durable recurring stream once gas turbines are shipped.

Why it continues: hyperscaler AI buildout is inelastic to GEV's pricing; the grid-upgrade backlog for HVDC and transformers is multi-year regardless of macro. GEV's only scaled competition in gas turbines is Siemens Energy and Mitsubishi — no new entrant can build that manufacturing capacity in years.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

The AI energy thesis is as directly applicable here as anywhere in the field. Power IS the binding constraint, and GEV is the picks-and-shovels supplier. Q1 2026 results confirmed the thesis is accelerating, not decelerating:

  • Orders +71% organic to $18.3B — not a one-quarter fluke; driven by both gas turbine reservations and electrification
  • Backlog at record $163B (+$13B sequential), now targeting $200B by 2027 (one year ahead of prior plan)
  • Gas turbine slots filling through 2030: pricing power is locked in for years, not quarters
  • Guidance raised to $44.5–45.5B revenue / 12–14% adj. EBITDA / $6.5–7.5B FCF for 2026

The question isn't whether GEV is a great business — it demonstrably is. The question is whether $939 is a good entry. That's encouraging for the business but doesn't resolve the valuation question: at ~37x 2026 FCF, you are paying for the continued strong execution of an already-proven story.

Research dossier: SITM — SiTime Corporation

Researched: 2026-07-04 · Verdict: HOLD · Conviction: 0.62 · Opportunity score: 41

Business

SiTime makes MEMS-based precision timing semiconductors — oscillators and (post-Renesas) clock

ICs that are the heartbeat of virtually all electronics. MEMS timing is a structural upgrade

over quartz: smaller, lower power, superior jitter, no piezoelectric aging. SiTime is the

dominant pure-play with ~60% of the MEMS timing market. Revenue is led by Communications,

Enterprise & Datacenter (CED), up ~158% YoY in Q1 2026; AI/datacenter is the primary engine —

as inference clusters densify (PCIe 5/6, 800G/1.6T Ethernet, high-radix switching), timing

tightness rises, so higher GPU density = more MEMS content per rack.

What's new since the 2026-06-27 dive: the Renesas timing-business acquisition **closed on

2026-07-01** — materially earlier than the "year-end 2026" close previously guided. SiTime now

owns the ~$300M-revenue, ~70%-gross-margin, ~75%-AI-Datacenter-Comms clock business outright: a

new $200M senior secured revolving credit facility (Wells Fargo, closed June 30) sits alongside

the $1.2B 0% convert (May) and the $900M term loan as the funding stack; Renesas received ~4.13M

SiTime shares (now outstanding, with registration rights) plus a board seat for CEO Shibata.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

The underlying business quality is undisputed and, if anything, strengthened: the deal that was

an open integration risk two weeks ago is now closed six months ahead of schedule, converting a

"pending, financed" story into a "done, operating" one. That is a real de-risking event, not

just a data point — the two biggest tail risks in the 06-27 dossier (deal falls through / slips

into 2027; the debt stack sits unused for months) are both resolved in the bull's favor.

The market's reaction was the opposite of a re-rate up: -14.6% (to $601.66) on 07-02, then

another leg down, bringing the stock to $601.57 by today (screen), a -15.7% 20-day return

and now sitting -12.5% below its 50DMA (was -0.4% on 06-27) and +39.6% over the 200DMA

(down from +58.8%). Searches found no fresh negative business fact behind the drop — no guidance

cut, no lost design win. The likeliest read (consistent with the 06-27 QuiverQuant framing that

called this an ongoing "financing overhang" story, now crystallizing at close): the market is

pricing the immediate, concrete dilution — 4.13M shares now actually outstanding rather than

a future contingency, registration rights for Renesas to sell into the market, and a fully drawn

leverage stack ($1.2B convert + $900M term loan + new $200M revolver) — against a business that

was already trading at ~47x trailing sales. Closing early removes integration-timeline risk but

crystallizes the dilution/leverage the market had been discounting only partially.

Per extended-with-vs-without-catalyst: is this a fresh catalyst or a re-confirmation? The

deal closing on-thesis, just early, is confirmation of the standing bull case, not a new one —

but the price reaction is real and moves the entry math. This is now the **best entry point

since the deal was announced in February** — genuinely closer to the $560-660 fair band this

desk derived two weeks ago, not just a shallow pullback from an already-rich price.

Conclusion: still HOLD, but the case for BUY is meaningfully closer than two weeks ago. At

$601.57 the stock sits mid-fair-band rather than at the top of it. This isn't yet the "real

dip" the base rates and macro stance want (33.2% off the 52-week high is just outside the

15-30% dip_buyer preset window — close, not there), and there's no confirmed fresh insider-

buying signal to offset the standing insider-selling overhang (no July Form 4s found in this

search; the most recent located sales are June 3-4 officer sales and the May 14 MegaChips

400K-share block sale at $779.50 — a 10%-owner distributing, which is a bigger tell than the

officer-level sales flagged last run). Absent a confirmed insider buy or a print, this is a

name to keep on a short leash for a trigger-gated add, not a buy-the-post-close-dip trade today.

Business

The world's dominant pure-play foundry — it manufactures the leading-edge logic (and increasingly the advanced packaging) that everyone else designs. Customers are the fabless ecosystem: NVIDIA, Apple, AMD, Broadcom, Qualcomm. Revenue durably continues because TSM is a near-monopoly at the leading edge (3nm/2nm) and the binding bottleneck of the AI buildout. This is the "wafers" half of Gavin Baker's "watts and wafers" — and per Nvidia - AI Cycle Durability and GPU Economics, TSM's restraint (disciplined capacity adds run by "flinty old-school veterans") is what smooths and elongates the cycle by preventing an overbuild. Wafer intensity may be AI's savior; TSM is the toll booth.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

Research dossier: BTDR — Bitdeer Technologies Group

Researched: 2026-06-20 · Verdict: HOLD · Conviction: 0.5 · Opportunity score: 38

Next earnings: 2026-08-12

Business

Bitdeer Technologies Group (NASDAQ: BTDR) is a Bitcoin miner executing a funded pivot into AI/HPC data-center infrastructure. Founded by Jihan Wu (Bitmain co-founder). Three revenue legs: (1) self-mining BTC — still the dominant engine (70.2 EH/s self-mining hashrate, 83.1 EH/s under management as of May 2026); (2) mining hosting / cloud hashrate; (3) AI Cloud — early GPU colocation + cloud (ARR ~$69M at 90% utilization, 4,248 GPUs deployed). It designs its own ASICs (SEALMINER line; A4 at 9.45 J/T, plus the DL1 Hydro Scrypt rig) for internal use and sale — the in-house silicon is a genuine cost edge over miners buying third-party rigs.

The durable differentiator is power-advantaged sites inside a stated ~3GW global power portfolio: Norway (Tydal — Phase 1 50MW + Phase 2 175MW, hydro, Nvidia Vera Rubin reference design, both phases now targeted for Q4-2026 energization) and a 570MW Clarington, Ohio site (power under contract with AEP). Management has explicitly reframed the story: colocation, not BTC appreciation, is the compounding bet, and "executing colocation lease agreements" is named top priority.

Why AI-colocation revenue would durably continue: cheap Norwegian hydro + EU data-sovereignty pull create real demand for EU-based AI compute. The open question is unchanged across three dives now — the anchor customer is still unsigned, so pricing power and customer quality remain unconfirmed.

Fresh thesis — is this a good buy now?

**Still pre-customer, and the net of the last 7 days is mixed-to-slightly-negative. The Tydal tenant is "in advanced negotiations" — but that exact phrase appeared in both the May and June updates, so the headline fact hasn't actually advanced. Meanwhile Clarington just picked up a fresh negative (litigation delay). Neither the "fresh-catalyst" nor the "real-dip" gate is open.**

This is a textbook Wait-for-deal thesis structure: power-rich, Nvidia-aligned sites ahead of a signed hyperscaler/AI-lab anchor. If a named customer signs the Tydal lease this reprices hard (the BE-post-Oracle "sustained repricing" pattern is the analog). Applying extended-with-vs-without-catalyst's operational test — what fact about the business changed in the last 7–14 days? — the honest answer:

  • Tydal: still "advanced negotiations," no signature. The language is now a month stale; protracted negotiation without close is a mild yellow flag, not a catalyst.
  • Clarington (NEW, negative): the 570MW Ohio site is delayed by legal proceedings filed by a neighboring company (American Heavy Plate Solutions LLC); no energization timeline given. This narrows the near-term colocation surface to Tydal alone.
  • Production: 921 BTC mined in May (+370% YoY), record hashrate — strong operational color, but mining is the gross-margin-negative leg, so volume isn't the value driver.

So the run (+35% 20d, +118% 60d, +30% vs 200DMA) is momentum without a thesis-confirming fact — the FOMO frame is the correct one. Don't chase.

Fundamentals remain uncomfortable: Q1 gross margin was -20.7% (deteriorated from -5.7% a year ago), Q1 net loss $159.5M, TTM net income -$199M. The company upsized its February convertible to $375M of 5.00% notes due 2032 (larger than the ~$325M I carried last dive) — a real dilutive/cash-cost overhang. The Q1 revenue beat ($188.9M, +169% YoY) is top-line growth, not an earnings inflection; profitability is still negative at the gross line.

Valuation + position vs. range

Price: $17.93 · 52-week range: ~$6.92 – ~$27.7 · Position in range: ~65% of high (35% off the high; +159% off the low)

  • Market cap: $4.36B (243.31M shares — confirmed via stockanalysis.com).
  • TTM revenue: $739M (+146% YoY). P/S ≈ 5.9×. For a gross-margin-negative mining base this is the wrong lens and not cheap — you're paying a forward AI-colocation multiple on a business that doesn't yet earn it.
  • Debt: ~$375M 5.00% convertibles (2032) + prior tranches; interest cost and dilution overhang are a headwind, not noise.
  • Sell-side: consensus "Strong Buy," avg PT ~$21.52 (~+20%) — note the Street is already leaning bullish, which tempers the contrarian edge.

AI-Cloud prize (unchanged math): Tydal at full 225MW (50+175), even at conservative colocation rates, could add ~$150–220M ARR at full occupancy — multiples of the current ~$69M AI-Cloud ARR. That is the entire bull case, and it is contingent on a customer that does not yet exist.

  • Pattern read (2026-07-09, LLM-authored): Read notes hinge on an open-ended market condition (a price band, catalyst, or event still pending) with a range-based check that stays relevant across many future runs. Died-unread notes are single-fire action items tied to a specific missed moment ("market was closed," "deferred this exact order") whose trigger is just "next session" — a narrow, time-perishable window rather than a persisting condition. Once that one imminent open-and-execute opportunity passes, the note has nothing left to match against, so it expires unread instead of being re-surfaced.

_Descriptive self-observation, regenerated nightly from that night's note fates (never appended, never accumulated) — evidence about the FORM of notes that land vs die, never a command._

AVGO-2026-07-10-hold-on-drift›

AVGO — HOLD on drift-consumed entry (research_verdict signal)

Decision

  • Action: HOLD (no order)
  • Signal: 2026-07-09:AVGO:research:buy (research_verdict, severity 4, opportunity 55, conviction 0.58)
  • Entry price marked: $399.68 (live quote, 2026-07-10T14:01:58Z)
  • Confidence: 0.55
  • Time: 2026-07-10, decide run

Reasoning

The research dossier (run 2026-06-30) rated AVGO BUY at $377.75 off a fresh, thesis-confirming

catalyst — OpenAI's Jalapeño ASIC deal (announced Jun 24, ~10GW deployment 2H26–2029) — landing

into a name still ~24% off its ATH and not yet re-rated on the news. Its own entry ladder: buy-here

(first tranche) ≤$385, add zone $345–355, fair $400–415, don't-chase above $440.

Ten days later the live price is $399.68 — +5.8% since the dossier, already above the $385

buy-here gate and sitting at the floor of the fair-value band. The margin to fair has compressed

from 6–11% to roughly 0–5%. The catalyst itself is now 16 days old — no longer fresh by the

extended-with-vs-without-catalyst framework's own standard, and the price action shows the market

has since done exactly the re-rating the dossier said hadn't happened yet. Buying here isn't buying

the de-rated setup the dossier argued for; it's chasing the same catalyst after the market already

priced a chunk of it.

Cross-rank: AVGO is #16/126 (opp 55), still respectable, but with $1.59 cash a real position

requires a rotation. No held name clears both gates (min-hold passed AND weak enough to justify

displacing) for an entry whose edge is already mostly gone — funding a marginal buy by selling a

sound thesis-intact position to chase a name that's run past its own stated entry ladder is the

wrong trade twice over.

Entry shape

Not "wait for a level" in the passive sense — the dossier already gave the level ($385 first

tranche, $345–355 high-conviction add) and price ran past the first one before this run could act

on it. No timing edge invented here; deferring to the pre-existing ladder rather than chasing the

gap.
